discussion_comments.comment_body: `BifrostContextKeyProviderOverride` cannot be added to `reservedKeys`. Bifrost itself writes to this key via `ctx.SetValue` inside both `tryRequest` and `tryStreamRequest` after each `PreLLMHook` run. Adding it to `reservedKeys` would cause those internal writes to be silently dropped when `blockRestrictedWrites` is enabled — breaking the override mechanism. Plugins cannot usefully set this key directly either: Bifrost unconditionally overwrites it from `preReq.ProviderOverride` on every dispatch. Updated the comment to make this reasoning explicit.

**Finding 1 (High, blocking): masked values still persist when the old key lacks the section or field.**

Every nested block is gated on `oldRedactedKey.X != nil && oldRawKey.X != nil` (here, and at lines 367, 382), and optional pointer fields additionally require the old field to be non-nil (e.g. Bedrock SessionToken at 389-394). Since `mergedKey := updateKey`, when a gate fails the incoming masked value is persisted verbatim: `updateProviderKey` validates only Value-emptiness afterwards and `UpdateProviderKey` writes the key as-is.

Concrete trigger: `PUT .../keys/{id}` with `"bedrock_key_config": {"session_token": "ABCD************************WXYZ", ...}` while the stored key has no SessionToken (stale UI render from before the token was cleared, or a payload copied from another key). The mask is stored as the literal session token, reproducing the #4353 corruption class this PR closes for the other paths.

Suggested shape:
```go
// after the per-field preserve guards, for each nested masked non-secret
// value with no stored counterpart, fail loudly instead of persisting:
if updateKey.BedrockKeyConfig != nil && updateKey.BedrockKeyConfig.SessionToken != nil &&
    updateKey.BedrockKeyConfig.SessionToken.IsRedacted() && !updateKey.BedrockKeyConfig.SessionToken.IsFromSecret() &&
    (oldRawKey.BedrockKeyConfig == nil || oldRawKey.BedrockKeyConfig.SessionToken == nil) {
    return ..., errMaskedPreviewWithoutStoredValue // -> 400
}
```
(or centralize this in the shared helper suggested in the other comment, applied unconditionally to the update payload).

Fixed in `eebf54f87`. Masked placeholders now require a non-empty stored counterpart. Missing config sections, missing optional fields, and empty stored values return HTTP 400 before persistence. Regression tests cover all three cases.

Fixed — applied the bypass pattern you suggested:

1. `BifrostContextKeyStreamGated` is now in `reservedKeys` (`core/schemas/context.go:28`).
2. Added a private `setReservedValue(key, value any)` method that mirrors `SetValue`'s `valueDelegate` recursion exactly but skips the `blockRestrictedWrites + reservedKeys` check. Lowercase-prefixed for package-internal access only — plugins can never see or call it.
3. `PauseStream` / `ResumeStream` / `EndStream` now use `bc.setReservedValue(BifrostContextKeyStreamGated, true)` instead of the public `SetValue` path.

Net effect: a plugin calling `bc.SetValue(BifrostContextKeyStreamGated, false)` directly is now silently dropped (consistent with how every other reserved key works), while the framework-internal Pause/Resume/End helpers continue to engage the gate from plugin scopes. Verified — core/schemas: 280 tests pass; framework gate suite: 33 tests pass. Please verify and resolve.

+// metadata addresses rejected regardless of allowPrivateNetwork) are

+func validateWebhookEndpointURL(rawURL string, allowPrivateNetwork bool) error {

+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL cannot be empty")
+	}

+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("invalid webhook URL: %w", err)
+	}
+	if parsed.Scheme == "http" && !allowPrivateNetwork {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL must use https (http requires allow_private_network)")
+	}
+	if parsed.User != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL must not contain credentials")
+	}
+	if parsed.Fragment != "" {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL must not contain a fragment")
+	}
+	return bifrost.ValidateExternalURL(rawURL, allowPrivateNetwork)

+	if w == nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook endpoint cannot be nil")
+	}
+	if w.Name == "" {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook endpoint name cannot be empty")
+	}
+	if err := validateWebhookEndpointURL(w.URL, w.AllowPrivateNetwork); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if len(w.Events) == 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook endpoint must subscribe to at least one event")
+	}
+	seen := make(map[WebhookEvent]bool, len(w.Events))
+	for _, event := range w.Events {
+		if !event.IsValid() {
+			return fmt.Errorf("unknown webhook event %q", event)
+		}
+		if seen[event] {
+			return fmt.Errorf("duplicate webhook event %q", event)
+		}
+		seen[event] = true
+	}
+	for name, value := range map[string]int{
+		"max_retries":                   w.MaxRetries,
+		"retry_backoff_initial_seconds": w.RetryBackoffInitialSeconds,
+		"retry_backoff_max_seconds":     w.RetryBackoffMaxSeconds,
+		"attempt_timeout_seconds":       w.AttemptTimeoutSeconds,
+		"max_response_payload_kbs":      w.MaxResponsePayloadKBs,
+		"max_concurrent_deliveries":     w.MaxConcurrentDeliveries,
+	} {
+		if value < 0 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("webhook endpoint %s must be positive when set", name)
+		}
+	}
+	for name := range w.Headers {
+		if !isValidHeaderName(name) {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid webhook header name %q", name)
+		}
+		if IsProtectedWebhookHeader(name) {
+			return fmt.Errorf("webhook header %q is reserved and cannot be overridden", name)
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// validateWebhookEndpointURL validates a webhook delivery URL. HTTPS is
+// required unless allowPrivateNetwork is set (which also unlocks private
+// address ranges for LAN/cluster receivers); URLs must not carry credentials
+// or fragments. Scheme allowlisting and IP-range checks (link-local and
+// metadata addresses rejected regardless of allowPrivateNetwork) are
+// delegated to bifrost.ValidateExternalURL.
+func validateWebhookEndpointURL(rawURL string, allowPrivateNetwork bool) error {
+	if rawURL == "" {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL cannot be empty")
+	}
+	parsed, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("invalid webhook URL: %w", err)
+	}
+	if parsed.Scheme == "http" && !allowPrivateNetwork {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL must use https (http requires allow_private_network)")
+	}
+	if parsed.User != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL must not contain credentials")
+	}
+	if parsed.Fragment != "" {
+		return fmt.Errorf("webhook URL must not contain a fragment")
+	}
+	return bifrost.ValidateExternalURL(rawURL, allowPrivateNetwork)
discussion_comments.comment_body: Create-time URL validation is best-effort UX only — the enforcement point is dial time, where `network.SSRFSafeDialContext` re-resolves and rejects loopback/private/link-local on every dial (including redirects and pool re-dials). That's the only sound layer anyway: DNS rebinding makes any create-time check bypassable. So `https://127.0.0.1/...` may save, but every delivery fails at dial unless `allow_private_network` is set. The HTTP↔private coupling is deliberate: plaintext HTTP is only acceptable to in-network receivers, which is exactly what the flag declares — a separate `allow_http` knob would just be a second name for the same trust decision.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Good catch — fixed in [959c8a5](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/pull/2054/commits/959c8a55b8d8521016be243f3030bac32765ee92).

Switched to `u.Hostname()` (which strips the port) before the suffix check, so URLs like `https://api.githubcopilot.com:443` from enterprise / proxied Copilot deployments are no longer silently rejected. Also added two regression fixtures in `utils_test.go` covering `:443` and `:8443` host:port forms.

These four returns are reached only after the JWT has already verified successfully — the credential is valid. They signal VK-state problems (deleted/inactive key) or server-side faults (`configStore == nil`, server build failure), not missing/invalid credentials.

RFC 9728 §5.1 scopes `WWW-Authenticate` to requests made "without authentication credentials or with invalid credentials," which does not apply post-verification. Emitting it here would push MCP clients into a pointless OAuth re-auth that mints another valid token failing identically, and would mask the real error (e.g. "virtual key is inactive"). For the server-fault cases it would be actively misleading.

The sibling paths that set the header are all genuine authentication failures (bad/expired token, missing VK header, session-mode rejection when auth is enforced), so the behavior is intentionally different here.

+// count_tokens path on the Bedrock Mantle endpoint.

+// Claude-specific and AWS rejects other models on it, while the OpenAI-compatible mantle surface
+// exposes no count-tokens path at all. Non-Anthropic models therefore get the standard

+// action to a Bedrock Project resource.

+		req.Header.Set(anthropic.AnthropicBetaHeader, strings.Join(betaHeaders, ","))

+	}

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed, though not with the suggested patch - unconditionally sending `jsonBody` would have been incorrect here.

In large payload mode the router skips body parsing entirely (`integrations/router.go:709-712`) and only `hydrateAnthropicRequestFromLargePayloadMetadata` runs, which sets `Model` and `Stream` and nothing else. So the converted `jsonBody` carries no messages in that mode - sending it would trade a 403 for a 400 (or a meaningless count).

The actual defect was narrower: only the signature was wrong. `req.Body()` drains a fasthttp body stream into the request buffer (`fasthttp/http.go:449-466`), so materializing it before signing makes the signed bytes and the sent bytes identical:

```go
signedBody := jsonBody
if usedLargePayloadBody {
    signedBody = req.Body()
}
sigHeaders, signErr := signer(signedBody)
```

The API-key path keeps streaming - there is no signature to invalidate, and the raw body is the only place the real messages live. A `max_tokens` in a body the client posted to `/v1/messages/count_tokens` earns a 400 that is correctly attributable to the caller; silently rewriting a passthrough body would be the surprising behaviour.

Added `TestCountTokensSignsTheBodyItSends` to pin the fasthttp draining behaviour the fix depends on.

Note for follow-up: `anthropic.completeRequest` (`core/providers/anthropic/anthropic.go:241-253`) has the identical pattern and is what the Bedrock Mantle *chat* surface uses via `HandleAnthropicChatCompletionRequest` + `mantleSigner`, so the same 403 is latent there. Not touched in this PR.

+// parseMantleAnthropicError parses an error response from the Bedrock Mantle native-Anthropic
+// surface. Errors there follow the Anthropic envelope
+// ({"type":"error","error":{"type":...,"message":...}}) rather than the AWS JSON error shape
+// that bedrock-runtime returns, so the Anthropic error type is what must be unmarshalled.
+func parseMantleAnthropicError(resp *fasthttp.Response) *schemas.BifrostError {
+	var errorResp anthropic.AnthropicError
+	bifrostErr := providerUtils.HandleProviderAPIError(resp, &errorResp)
+	if errorResp.Error != nil {
+		if bifrostErr.Error == nil {
+			bifrostErr.Error = &schemas.ErrorField{}
+		}
+		bifrostErr.Error.Type = &errorResp.Error.Type
+		bifrostErr.Error.Message = errorResp.Error.Message
+	}
+	return bifrostErr
+}
+
+// CountTokens counts the input tokens a request would consume, using the native-Anthropic
+// count_tokens path on the Bedrock Mantle endpoint.
+//
+// Only Anthropic-family (Claude) models are supported: the /anthropic/v1/messages surface is
+// Claude-specific and AWS rejects other models on it, while the OpenAI-compatible mantle surface
+// exposes no count-tokens path at all. Non-Anthropic models therefore get the standard
+// unsupported-operation error rather than a request that is guaranteed to fail upstream.
+//
+// Auth mirrors the other mantle surfaces: a Bedrock Mantle API key flows through the
+// Authorization header, otherwise the exact body bytes are SigV4-signed for the bedrock-mantle
+// service. The project header is sent because AWS scopes the bedrock-mantle:CountTokens IAM
+// action to a Bedrock Project resource.
+func (provider *BedrockMantleProvider) CountTokens(ctx *schemas.BifrostContext, key schemas.Key, request *schemas.BifrostResponsesRequest) (*schemas.BifrostCountTokensResponse, *schemas.BifrostError) {
+	if !schemas.IsAnthropicModelFamily(ctx, request.Model) {
+		return nil, providerUtils.NewUnsupportedOperationError(schemas.CountTokensRequest, provider.GetProviderKey())
+	}
+
+	region := provider.resolveRegion(ctx, key, request.Model)
+	url := mantleAnthropicCountTokensURL(region)
+	_, bareModel := parseBedrockRegionAndModel(request.Model)
+
+	// IsCountTokens keeps the model field (mantle routes on it) and strips max_tokens /
+	// temperature / fallback_credit_token, which the count_tokens schema rejects. ExcludeFields
+	// repeats max_tokens and temperature so they are also removed on the typed path, matching
+	// the shared Anthropic count-tokens handler.
+	jsonBody, bifrostErr := anthropic.BuildAnthropicResponsesRequestBody(ctx, request, anthropic.AnthropicRequestBuildConfig{
+		Provider:                  schemas.BedrockMantle,
+		Model:                     bareModel,
+		IsCountTokens:             true,
+		IsStreaming:               false,
+		ValidateTools:             true,
+		ExcludeFields:             []string{"max_tokens", "temperature"},
+		BetaHeaderOverrides:       provider.networkConfig.BetaHeaderOverrides,
+		ShouldSendBackRawRequest:  provider.sendBackRawRequest,
+		ShouldSendBackRawResponse: provider.sendBackRawResponse,
+	})
+	if bifrostErr != nil {
+		return nil, bifrostErr
+	}
+
+	req := fasthttp.AcquireRequest()
+	resp := fasthttp.AcquireResponse()
+	defer fasthttp.ReleaseRequest(req)
+	defer fasthttp.ReleaseResponse(resp)
+
+	req.SetRequestURI(url)
+	req.Header.SetMethod(http.MethodPost)
+
+	extraHeaders := addAnthropicHeaders(bedrock.WithMantleProject(provider.networkConfig.ExtraHeaders, bedrock.MantleAnthropicProjectHeader, resolveProjectID(ctx, key)))
+	providerUtils.SetExtraHeaders(ctx, req, extraHeaders, []string{anthropic.AnthropicBetaHeader})
+
+	// Force JSON content type after extra headers so network config cannot override it.
+	req.Header.SetContentType("application/json")
+
+	if betaHeaders := anthropic.FilterBetaHeadersForProvider(anthropic.MergeBetaHeaders(ctx, extraHeaders), schemas.BedrockMantle, provider.networkConfig.BetaHeaderOverrides); len(betaHeaders) > 0 {
+		req.Header.Set(anthropic.AnthropicBetaHeader, strings.Join(betaHeaders, ","))
+	} else {
+		req.Header.Del(anthropic.AnthropicBetaHeader)
+	}
+
+	// Apply auth headers last so they win over network-config headers.
+	for headerKey, headerValue := range openai.BearerAuthHeader(key) {
+		req.Header.Set(headerKey, headerValue)
+	}
+
+	// Keep one request-body path for both modes: normal mode sends the converted JSON, large
+	// payload mode streams the original client body reader instead of duplicating it in memory.
+	usedLargePayloadBody := providerUtils.ApplyLargePayloadRequestBodyWithModelNormalization(ctx, req, schemas.BedrockMantle)
+	if !usedLargePayloadBody {
+		req.SetBody(jsonBody)
+	}
+
+	// Sign after the body is set so the SigV4 signature covers exactly what is sent. The signer
+	// is nil when a Bedrock Mantle API key is configured (auth is the Authorization header then).
+	if signer := provider.mantleSigner(ctx, key, url, "application/json", region); signer != nil {
+		sigHeaders, signErr := signer(jsonBody)
+		if signErr != nil {
+			return nil, signErr
+		}
+		for headerKey, headerValue := range sigHeaders {
+			req.Header.Set(headerKey, headerValue)
+		}

Follow-up: this fix has moved. Per the review thread below, `bedrockmantle.CountTokens` now routes through the shared `anthropic.HandleAnthropicCountTokensRequest`, so the signed-body fix lives in `anthropic.completeRequest` rather than in this file - the code you commented on no longer exists here.

Same behaviour, one level up:

```go
signedBody := jsonBody
if usedLargePayloadBody {
    signedBody = req.Body()
}
sigHeaders, bErr := signer(signedBody)
```

Relocating it also fixed the identical latent issue on the Bedrock Mantle chat surface, which goes through the same `completeRequest` with a signer.
